pr93_lows.claim: A phone written right after another number is still missed. This is what remains of R2. First, gluedPhoneRun (line 508) skips a run when a digit comes before ','. So a CSV row whose phone column follows a numeric column passes decideNotebookWrite and is stored. Second, phoneRun (line 501) merges a number of three or more digits, one space or tab, and the phone into a single run of more than 13 digits, which is not phone-shaped.
pr93_lows.evidence: screenCustomerText and decideNotebookWrite let each of these through: "order_number,phone\n1042,03001234567", "#1042,+923001234567", "Order 1042,+14155552671", "1042 03001234567" and "1042\t03001234567". The earlier module also let them through.
pr93_lows.fix: In the glued pass, allow a digit before ',' or a tab when the run is strongly phone-shaped: it starts with '+', or it has 10 or 11 digits with a trunk 0. When a run of several groups fails phoneShaped, test its suffix again from each group boundary that follows a space or tab (at most 16 boundaries). Pin both CSV rows in the phones test.

pr93_lows.claim: Reading link contents (lines 1194-1199, linkContent at line 468) adds a deterministic false positive. A bare query value or path segment of 10 or 11 digits that is shaped like a North American number is read as a phone. Google Sheets tab links and legacy-id admin links are therefore refused; the earlier module passed them.
pr93_lows.evidence: 11,018 of 200,000 random 'https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1AbC/edit#gid=N' links (5.5%) are refused as phone. So is 'https://admin.shopify.com/store/my-shop/collections/2612345678'. A knowledge.propose of kind supplier whose text cites a #gid=2063456789 sheet link returns refused customer_data. The screen fails closed, so nothing leaks.
pr93_lows.fix: Inside a link's content, read a value glued to '=' as a phone only after a phone key (phone, tel, mobile, whatsapp) or when it is strongly phone-shaped ('+', '00' or a trunk 0). Treat a bare path segment or any other query value as an id. Pin a sheet link and a collection link in the pass list.

pr93_lows.claim: Double percent-encoding is not decoded: percentEscapes and percentEscape (lines 164-175) have no %25. linkContent decodes it, but only the phone and address scans read its output. Links without a scheme are not read either: linkPattern (line 431) needs https:// or www.
pr93_lows.evidence: These pass: "jane%2540example.com", a login link whose return_url holds "email%3Djane%2540example.com", "gid%253A%252F%252Fshopify%252FCustomer%252F7234567890123", "maps.google.com/?q=221B+Baker+Street" and "maps.apple.com/?q=12+Main+St". "jane&#64;example.com" is caught, and the brief says escapes are decoded up to three times.
pr93_lows.fix: Add '25' -> '%' to percentEscapes and percentEscape; the three-pass loop already decodes again. Alternatively, run scanEmails and scanCustomerIds on each decoded link content. Extend linkPattern to a bare host with a top-level domain followed by '/' or '?'. Pin these forms in the tests.

pr93_lows.claim: The textChars and totalChars bounds (lines 1181-1184) are checked on the raw length. Every scan reads the NFKC fold, which can be up to 18 times longer (U+FDFA), so the stated time bound per mebibyte does not hold.
pr93_lows.evidence: '1 ' followed by 1 MiB of U+FDFA folds to 18.9M characters and took 17.7 s at load about 200. The brief says one to ten seconds. The linear-time test has no shape that expands under NFKC. Today's callers keep texts at 8,192 characters or fewer, which is about 0.3 s.
pr93_lows.fix: Check the folded length against textChars and totalChars and throw CUSTOMER_SCREEN_TEXT_TOO_LONG when it is over. Add a U+FDFA shape to the linear-time test.
